# Independent audit: triangle-frustum active-normal qualification obstruction

Source:
`candidate 29c345ef7c2b94ab`.


active-normal menu, the quadratic vertical depth germ, and the energy
gradient conclusion check. The example is OC-safe and only refutes an
unqualified active-normal KKT inference.

## 1. Actual geometry and triangle slices

The inequalities defining x in (1+epsilon t)T are affine in (x,t),
and 1+epsilon t>0 on the whole stated height interval. Thus the body
is full-dimensional and convex. For any nonzero horizontal covector,
its maximum vertex value is positive; scaling it to two and sorting
the remaining values yields exactly (2,-R,R-2), 1<=R<=4. This includes
all horizontal orientations and the tied-height endpoints R=1,4.

The isolated-maximum cap formula has denominator
D=(R+2)(4-R), and the lower complementary cap has denominator
E=(R+2)(2R-2). The two branches meet continuously. The density peak
2/(R+2) is the correct normalized one-dimensional marginal density.
Formula (4)'s difference from one half is exactly
(R-2)/[(R+2)(2R-2)]. No Euclidean-normal normalization factor is
missing: all thresholds use the same scaled covector.

## 2. An elementary triangle paired-tail proof

The source cites an already proved paired-tail theorem. Its needed
triangle case also has the following direct proof, so no localization
dependency is necessary for this counterexample.

Let q>=0. For 1<R<2 and 0<=q<=2-R, both tails isolate the top
vertex and their sum is (8+2q^2)/D>=8/9. On 2-R<=q<=R it is

             J(q)=1+(2-q)^2/D-(R-q)^2/E.

This quadratic is concave because E<=D. Its endpoints are at least
8/9: the first agrees with the previous interval, the second is
1+F(R)>=1. Beyond q=R the negative-threshold tail is one, so the
sum is at least one.

For 2<R<4, the sum on 0<=q<=R-2 is
2-2(R^2+q^2)/E and decreases to the mixed interval. On R-2<=q<=2
the same J is convex and has its minimum at q=(R+2)/3, with value

        2(R+4)/[3(R+2)]=8/9+2(4-R)/[9(R+2)]>=8/9.

From q=2 to q=R the positive-threshold tail is zero and the other
tail increases, so no smaller value occurs; afterwards the sum is one.
The cases R=1,2,4 follow directly or by continuity of actual triangle
cap volume as the normal varies, including support thresholds.
This proves the exact needed bound for every q and orientation.

## 3. The global away-normal gap

The product-body split covers every scaled normal. For |beta|>=72,
the fully captured height interval has probability at least 17/36.
For |beta|<=72 and s=R-1>=1/4, the through-zero triangle gap is at
least Delta=4/1287. The marginal Lipschitz bound loses at most
(4/3)|beta|t in the paired tails. On t<=Delta/96 it leaves paired
gap Delta; half the integral gives Delta^2/192.

For s<1/4 and 1/4<=|beta|<=72, the exact quadratic paired formula
on t<=1/(4|beta|) supplies gap 1/(1728|beta|), at least 1/124416.
Pure vertical normals have product mass one half. Hence the source's
uniform delta=1/(12*1287^2) works on the entire complement of its
three local direction neighborhoods, not just at finitely many normals.

## 4. Uniform perturbation and exact local caps

Under the product reference law, the unperturbed margin n.X+beta t
has density at most min(2/3,1/(2|beta|)). The actual margin changes
by at most epsilon(4+|beta|/3). The resulting band probability is
bounded by (17/3)epsilon, with the maximum exactly at |beta|=3/4
in the stated elementary bound. Changing to the actual r(t)^2 height
law adds at most (7/3)epsilon. Pure vertical caps obey the separate
epsilon/6 event-shift bound. Thus 8epsilon is uniform over ALL normals.
The strict comparison 8*10^-9<delta is correct.

In each remaining local neighborhood, the entire height interval
stays in the single isolated-vertex slice regime. The largest threshold
magnitude 7/24 is below the least negative vertex-height magnitude
3/8; the upper vertex is farther away. Thus integration of the
quadratic formula is exact, with no omitted saturation cell.
The two identities integral r(t)(t-epsilon/3)=0 and
integral(t-epsilon/3)^2=I_2/3 give precisely
(4+beta^2/3)/(9-s^2). Equality forces s=0 and beta=0. The outside
gap is strict. This proves both the global depth 4/9 and exactly the
three oriented active normals.

Any halfspace containing the source with boundary not through it
has strictly larger mass than its parallel through-source cap, since
the source is interior. Thus it adds no active orientation or offset.

## 5. Uniqueness and the exact missing-direction germ

For x!=0 one canonical horizontal form is positive. Its parallel cap
through the point captures strictly less than the axis cap in every
positive-area slice, including slices where its tail becomes empty.
For x=0 and t_0!=epsilon/3, the linear tilt coefficient is proportional
to 2(epsilon/3-t_0), so a sufficiently small signed tilt reduces mass.
The top and bottom supporting planes also handle the endpoint heights.
This proves uniqueness throughout the actual body.

The source-height Lipschitz estimate is uniform: for |beta|<=4 the
conditional horizontal density bound gives (16/3)|h|; for |beta|>=4
the conditional height coefficient has magnitude at least |beta|/2
and the height density is at most 9/8, giving (9/4)|h|. Thus 6|h|
suffices. The chosen h_0 preserves the exterior positive gap. The
local incidence bound persists, and completing the exact quadratic
4I_2-8beta h+beta^2 J_2 gives the printed formula (16), with its
optimizer strictly inside the local beta interval. This is therefore
the actual all-normal depth germ, not merely one cap's upper bound.

## 6. Energy qualification and mixed product

The full ordinary dimension is three, so the energy parameter exponent
is minus four and its spatial gradient is 4E times the minimizer.
The triangle permutation group has no fixed nonzero horizontal
covector. Its determinant moduli are one, so energy invariance plus
unique parameter attainment forces a vertical minimizer. The actual
centroid height 2epsilon/[3(1+epsilon^2/3)] exceeds epsilon/3. Hence
the parameter is nonzero, indeed positive by the objective derivative
at zero and strict convexity. The gradient is outside the horizontal
span of every active normal, although the deepest set is a singleton.
This is exactly the claimed missing-qualification obstruction.

For [0,1] times K_epsilon, finite base tilts isolate either full
continuous fiber. The mixed depth is exactly half the ordinary depth,
and a critical mixed cap must have a critical own trace and zero
other-fiber mass. All its continuous normals are therefore horizontal
in the frustum coordinates. No pure-base critical cap is missing.
The energy gradient still has a nonzero height coordinate, outside
that span. This product assertion is also exact and OC-safe.

I reran the source verifier: **449 exact checks PASS**. The independent
`supporting computation verify_triangle_frustum_actual_polygon_audit_two_sided.py` passes
**10,453 exact checks**. It clips actual triangles, partitions height
at every exact vertex-incidence value, and integrates the resulting
quadratic slice areas exactly. Thus it independently checks the product
gap, actual positive/negative tilted frustum caps, every local formula,
and the exact optimizing height germ. The general all-normal proof is
the explicit regional argument above, not this finite screen.
